content.comment_body: Hello experts, I have some sensors for my project that operate at 24VDC. They are NPN-type sensors with two connection wires; I believe these should be provided with an NPN-type input. Is it possible to use these sensors with a [product_name]? If 24VDC is connected to the p2-pin and 0VDC to the p1-pin, will there be 24VDC between inputs and 0V?

[user_name], The inputs can be selected as required. You may connect 24VDC to one wire of the sensor and the other wire to your input. Ensure that the 24VDC supplied to your sensor is the same as the one powering the [product_name]. Regards, [user_name] [url]
Also, what is the correct way to connect a 3-wire NPN sensor?

You can use NPN sensors, but NPN sensors typically switch on the negative side, which may not work as expected in the [product_name]. If you add a resistor (about 1000 Ohm) between the positive supply and the digital input of the [product_name], then connect the NPN sensor to that digital input and to the negative supply, it should function correctly. The resistor value depends on your sensor's characteristics. In the programming software ([product_name] programming tool), you'll need to invert the input logic, which is straightforward. If possible, use a PNP sensor—it can usually connect directly to the [product_name].
